title: Largest Volume Rectangle

statement.md: A depth chart is a histogram of $n$ bars of width 1 with heights $h_1, \dots, h_n$ side by side. A rectangle must lie under the bars: it covers a run of consecutive bars and its height is at most the shortest bar in that run.
Print the largest possible rectangle area.

constraints: $0 \le h_i \le 10^9$; the area can exceed 32 bits
hints: For each bar, how far can a rectangle of exactly that bar height extend left and right?
A stack of bars with increasing heights finds the nearest shorter bar on each side in one pass.
editorial: [{"type": "p", "md": "For every bar $i$, the widest rectangle of height $h_i$ extends until the nearest strictly shorter bar on each side. Scan left to right keeping a stack of indices with increasing heights. When a bar is shorter than the stack top, pop the top: its right limit is the current index and its left limit is the new top. A sentinel bar of height 0 at the end flushes the stack. Each bar is pushed and popped once, so the time is $O(n)$. The product needs 64-bit integers."}]

solutions.python:
import sys


def main():
    tok = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(tok[0])
    h = list(map(int, tok[1:1 + n])) + [0]
    st = []
    best = 0
    for i, v in enumerate(h):
        while st and h[st[-1]] >= v:
            height = h[st.pop()]
            left = st[-1] if st else -1
            best = max(best, height * (i - left - 1))
        st.append(i)
    print(best)


main()
